_comment: Public example only. Every value is null because this file must never carry real account data. Freshness is evaluated from each provider's or pool's own checked_at, never from a shared timestamp. Every window carries a role: BURST windows supply BOTH a utilization signal (stranded_capacity_risk) and a NEW_WORK defensive signal (burst_depletion_pressure - nearly spent AND not refilling soon); BUDGET windows supply conservation_pressure (scarcity), budget_expiry_opportunity, and - only from a MULTI-observation series, never a single snapshot - pace_pressure (long-horizon trajectory). The three defensive signals compose into one resource_pressure_rank (CLEAR/SOFT_PRESSURED/BUDGET_SCARCE); BUDGET absolute scarcity always outranks softer pressure. remaining_ratio and reset_at are the facts every reading is derived from; the derived NEAR/MEDIUM/FAR, HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW, NONE..CRITICAL and pace labels are never stored here. Trajectory evidence, when a runtime keeps it, is an optional per-entry pace_observations array of {checked_at, remaining_ratio, reset_at, reset_at_source?, remaining_confidence?, generation_id?}; a single snapshot always yields pace UNKNOWN. A legacy snapshot with no role reads short_window as BURST and weekly_window as BUDGET; the generic windows list is the way to describe a provider whose caps are not named that way. remaining_confidence may lower the confidence implied by source, never raise it. A real runtime/RESOURCE_STATE.json is gitignored and must use boolean availability.
